verdicts.claim: SceneKit (the whole framework, incl. SCNGeometrySource/SCNGeometryElement/SCNScene.write) is deprecated in iOS 26.0: 'SceneKit is deprecated, use RealityKit instead' (WWDC25 session 288). It still compiles and runs on the iOS 26 SDK (soft deprecation, maintenance mode), but new display code should target RealityKit: MeshDescriptor + MeshResource.generate (iOS 15+) or LowLevelMesh (iOS 18+, zero-copy Metal buffers) for the mesh, TextureResource(image: CGImage) or LowLevelTexture (iOS 18+, Metal-written) for atlas pages, shown in ARView/RealityView with UnlitMaterial or PhysicallyBasedMaterial.
verdicts.correction: Headline stands (SceneKit incl. SCNGeometrySource/SCNGeometryElement/SCNScene.write deprecatedAt iOS 26.0, soft deprecation; LowLevelMesh, LowLevelTexture iOS 18.0; MeshDescriptor iOS 15.0), but three API details are wrong. (1) LowLevelMesh has no closure-form replaceIndices(_:). CPU index writers: `@MainActor func withUnsafeMutableIndices(_ callback: (UnsafeMutableRawBufferPointer) -> Void)` and `@MainActor func replaceUnsafeMutableIndices(_ callback: (UnsafeMutableRawBufferPointer) -> Void)`; GPU: `@MainActor func replaceIndices(using commandBuffer: any MTLCommandBuffer) -> any MTLBuffer`. Vertex side: `withUnsafeMutableBytes(bufferIndex:_:)`, `replaceUnsafeMutableBytes(bufferIndex:_:)`, `replace(bufferIndex:using:) -> any MTLBuffer`. All iOS 18.0. (2) MeshResource(from: LowLevelMesh): the doc lists only `@MainActor @preconcurrency convenience init(from mesh: LowLevelMesh) async throws` (iOS 18.0), but the SDK also accepts a synchronous call: Apple's own LowLevelMesh overview sample calls `let resource = try MeshResource(from: lowLevelMesh)` inside a non-async `func triangleEntity() throws -> Entity`, and dozens of compiling projects do the same from non-async throwing functions (metal-by-example/metal-spatial-dynamic-mesh, computer-graphics-tools/examples `@MainActor func createMeshResource() throws -> MeshResource`, tattn/VRMKit). So both a sync (undocumented in the topic list) and an async overload exist. Rule for Mapper: in a synchronous @MainActor function write `try MeshResource(from: mesh)`; inside an async function write `try await MeshResource(from: mesh)` (Swift prefers the async overload in async contexts, so omitting await there is a compile error). Both calls must be on the MainActor. (3) `TextureResource.init(image cgImage: CGImage, withName resourceName: String? = nil, options: TextureResource.CreateOptions)` is iOS 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / visionOS 2.0, not iOS 13. It is documented as async throws, and like MeshResource(from:) it is also called synchronously with plain `try` in compiling code (VRMKit, iridiumtao/LoudPlantsInYourArea `func addIcon(...) throws`), so the same sync/async rule applies. The older `static func generate(from cgImage: CGImage, withName: String? = nil, options: TextureResource.CreateOptions) throws -> TextureResource` is iOS 15.0, deprecatedAt iOS 18.0 (compiles with a warning; avoid on an iOS 18 target). `TextureResource(from: LowLevelTexture)` iOS 18.0 as claimed. From the official-docs verifier I reject only the statement that MeshResource(from:) must be awaited; from the reality verifier I accept the both-overloads finding and extend it to TextureResource(image:options:).
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the official-docs verdict: upheld on replaceIndices (re-fetched lowlevelmesh.json: topic list has withUnsafeMutableIndices, replaceUnsafeMutableIndices(_:), replaceIndices(using:) -> any MTLBuffer, readIndices(using:), no closure replaceIndices) and on the TextureResource(image:withName:options:) iOS 18.0 availability (re-fetched its JSON: introducedAt iOS 18.0, async throws; generate(from:withName:options:) iOS 15.0 deprecatedAt 18.0). Overruled on 'must be awaited': re-fetched meshresource/init(from:).json shows only the async declaration, but the code sample embedded in the same lowlevelmesh.json overview calls `try MeshResource(from: lowLevelMesh)` in a non-async throwing function, and GitHub code search shows 65 hits for `try MeshResource(from:` including non-async throwing functions in compiling repos (metal-by-example/metal-spatial-dynamic-mesh, computer-graphics-tools/examples, ShapeShading/immersive-attractor, tattn/VRMKit). A call to an async-only initializer without await from a sync function cannot compile, so a synchronous overload exists in the SDK interface even though DocC shows one.

The claim as written is refuted because replaceIndices(_ closure:) does not exist and the iOS 13 version is wrong. Evidence re-checked this session: GitHub code search for `try MeshResource(from:` (65 Swift hits, several in non-async throwing functions, e.g. metal-by-example/metal-spatial-dynamic-mesh ContentView.swift, computer-graphics-tools/examples SceneMeshBuilder.swift) and for `try TextureResource(image:` (24 hits, several synchronous, one gated by `#available(macOS 15.0, iOS 18.0, *)` in eugenehp/rswift, confirming iOS 18.0). verdicts.claim: ModelIO on iOS exports OBJ (+MTL) and STL for sure (documented), USDC/USDA per community (canExportFileExtension returns true), but NOT usdz (canExportFileExtension("usdz") returns false), and USD export drops materials entirely (unanswered Apple forum 2023). OBJ export writes material scalars (Kd etc.); whether map_Kd is written from a URL-valued baseColor property is undocumented and unverified. Practical consequence: write OBJ + MTL (map_Kd atlas_0.jpg) with your own ~100-line writer, and produce USDZ either via SceneKit's SCNScene.write(to: url.usdz) (deprecated in 26 but functional) or your own usda + 64-byte-aligned stored-zip writer (usdz spec). ModelIO is still fine as an importer and for SCNGeometry/MDLMesh bridging.
verdicts.correction: Verifier upheld. Rely on: (a) `MDLAsset.canExportFileExtension(_:)` (iOS 9.0) documents only .obj and .stl ('Additional formats may be supported as well'); community reports usdz false and usdc/usda true, unconfirmed on iOS 18, so log it on device. (b) ModelIO DOES have an official USDZ packager on the deployment target: `class MDLUtility : NSObject` with `class func convert(toUSDZ inputURL: URL, writeTo outputURL: URL)` (ObjC `+convertToUSDZ:writeToURL:`), iOS 18.0, iPadOS 18.0, Mac Catalyst 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, visionOS 2.0, not deprecated. It returns Void and does not throw, so success must be checked by the output file existing, being non-empty and starting with the zip signature 'PK'. Input must be a USD layer or a SceneKit-written scene file, not OBJ and not .reality (Apple staff, forum thread 759333, Jul 2024). (c) Practical path: write your own usda (UsdPreviewSurface + UsdUVTexture pointing at atlas_0.jpg by relative path beside it), then MDLUtility.convert(toUSDZ:writeTo:); keep the hand-rolled 64-byte-aligned stored-zip usdz writer as the fallback (it is small, deterministic and testable off-device), and do not rely on SCNScene.write (deprecated 26.0). (d) OBJ: MDLAsset OBJ/MTL material output is unreliable (Kd reported dropped or written as white, map_Kd undocumented); write OBJ + MTL yourself as the claim already recommends. USD export via MDLAsset.export keeps scalar UsdPreviewSurface inputs but drops URL-valued texture properties (community), so 'drops materials entirely' is overstated. Apple forum thread 111061 dates from 2018, not 2023, and never tested usdz.
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the official-docs verdict: upheld. Re-fetched modelio/mdlutility/convert(tousdz:writeto:).json this session: declaration `class func convert(toUSDZ inputURL: URL, writeTo outputURL: URL)`, introducedAt iOS 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / tvOS 18.0 / visionOS 2.0, no deprecatedAt. Fresh evidence of intended use: an Apple engineer on developer.apple.com/forums/thread/759333 (Jul 2024) recommends MDLUtility convertToUSDZ:writeToURL: to turn a SceneKit-written scene file into usdz and states it does not accept .reality files. No third-party app was found calling it on a device: GitHub code search for convert(toUSDZ / convertToUSDZ finds only doc mirrors and a Linux reimplementation test, so real-device behavior (especially texture packaging and error reporting) is unproven and needs one device test with a fallback. Re-fetched canexportfileextension(_:).json: text names only .obj and .stl, consistent with both researcher and verifier. The claim's omission of MDLUtility changes the recommended USDZ path, and its forum date and 'drops materials entirely' details are wrong, so the claim as written is refuted.

open_question_answers.question: Exact per-frame cost of CIContext.jpegRepresentation / ImageIO decode of 1920x1440 on A15 (no published numbers; measure in the first build, expect 10-30 ms each).
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: in build 3 time CIContext.jpegRepresentation(of:colorSpace:options:) at quality 0.85 and CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex decode of one 1920x1440 frame (log mean/p95 ms over 50 frames and thermal state). Architecture choice independent of the number: keep JPEG encode off the ARSession delegate thread on a serial utility queue with a bounded keyframe budget (drop, never queue unbounded), and prefer storing keyframes as HEIC/JPEG only at selection time (roughly 1-2 fps), not every frame.

open_question_answers.question: Whether ModelIO's OBJ exporter writes map_Kd for a URL-valued baseColor MDLMaterialProperty on iOS 18 (unverified; own writer recommended regardless).
open_question_answers.answer: Not architecture-blocking: write OBJ + MTL (Kd 1 1 1, map_Kd atlas_0.jpg) with the app's own writer; community evidence (radcli14/ModelIO-to-RealityKit) says MDLAsset does not reliably write Kd and drops URL-valued material properties, so do not depend on ModelIO for OBJ materials. Optional device log: export a one-quad MDLAsset with a URL baseColor to .obj and dump the .mtl text.

open_question_answers.question: Whether MDLAsset.canExportFileExtension("usdz") is still false and "usdc" true on iOS 18/26 (last community confirmation 2018).
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: log MDLAsset.canExportFileExtension for "usdz", "usdc", "usda", "obj", "stl" in the capability probe on iOS 18.3.2 (and later iOS 26). Docs guarantee only obj and stl. It no longer drives the architecture: USDZ is produced by own usda + MDLUtility.convert(toUSDZ:writeTo:) (iOS 18.0+, check the output file exists and begins with 'PK'), with the own stored-zip writer as fallback.

open_question_answers.question: RealityKit V-origin for MeshDescriptor/LowLevelMesh UVs (community says bottom-left; confirm with the on-device UV test).
open_question_answers.answer: Likely bottom-left (v = 0 at the bottom of the image), so for an atlas written top-left (CoreGraphics/Metal) store v' = 1 - v in the RealityKit mesh; evidence is maxxfrazer/RealityGeometries issue #3 (textures came out mirrored until UVs were flipped). OBJ and USD (UsdUVTexture st) are also bottom-left, so one convention (v up) can be shared by the display mesh and all exports. needs device test: render a numbered 2x2 test atlas on a quad and confirm the '1' tile appears top-left.

open_question_answers.question: Whether captureHighResolutionFrame's ARFrame.camera.intrinsics/imageResolution are rescaled to the 12 MP image (undocumented).
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: on a captureHighResolutionFrame result log camera.imageResolution, CVPixelBufferGetWidth/Height(capturedImage) and camera.intrinsics, and compare with the preceding regular frame. No doc or forum answer found (Apple forum thread 827789, May 2026, asks about intrinsics changes and has no replies). Architecture rule that is safe either way: before projecting, scale fx, fy, ox, oy by (pixelBufferWidth / imageResolution.width) and (pixelBufferHeight / imageResolution.height), which is a no-op if ARKit already rescaled. Hi-res frames stay optional in v1.

open_question_answers.question: Whether Xcode 26.6 emits deprecation warnings for viewMatrix(for:)/projectPoint(_:orientation:viewportSize:) (docs say deprecated in iOS 27; irrelevant if the intrinsics formula is used).
open_question_answers.answer: Irrelevant to architecture: the texturing projector uses camera.transform.inverse plus camera.intrinsics directly, not viewMatrix(for:) or projectPoint(_:orientation:viewportSize:). The current ARCamera doc marks the orientation overloads (viewMatrixForOrientation:, projectPoint:orientation:viewportSize:) deprecated and adds viewRotationAngle: replacements; any warning in Xcode 26.6 is only a warning and the replacements must not be used on an iOS 18 target without #available.

open_question_answers.question: Typical triangle counts of ARMeshAnchor snapshots for large rooms on iPhone 13 Pro Max (community: ~100k-500k; measure) to decide whether decimation is needed before texturing.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: after a room scan log total ARMeshAnchor count, sum of geometry.faces.count and vertices.count, and memory footprint, for a small room, a large living room and a multi-room walk. Architecture decision to take now: make decimation (or per-chunk atlas budgeting) a pipeline stage that is a no-op below a triangle threshold (for example 300k) rather than a later retrofit, since atlas size and projection time scale with face count.
